parts.label: Part 4
parts.article:
Part 4. You will hear a professor of environmental biology talking about urban biodiversity. First, you have some time to look at questions thirty-one to forty on page seven.

Now listen carefully and answer questions thirty-one to forty.

Today I want to talk about urban biodiversity. That is the amazing variety of plant and animal life that we find in cities throughout the world. Cities are providing new opportunities for wildlife through habitats provided in spaces such as parks and empty, undeveloped lots. With some help from humans, species can be preserved despite living close to people. Sometimes species survive more successfully than in rural areas where they may be threatened by hunting. Though this is increasingly regulated by governments, another threat they face in rural areas is the ever-encroaching spread of farms and suburban housing, which reduces natural habitat significantly. Once you start to look, you will be amazed by the variety of life which exists side by side with people in cities. Look at the wildlife which share our buildings. There are moss and lichens on older buildings, and particularly numerous are the insects which find breeding places and shelter there. And urban environmentalists have for a long time been aware of the particular attraction of garden walls made of wood, stone, brick, and even concrete, which provide ideal spots for smaller plant and animal species to thrive.

Over time, many species that were initially crowded out from their habitats return to the sites of their original inhabitation. Now, in the heart of cities, this is particularly true in the case of birds. London is today home to the peregrine falcon, a bird once thought close to extinction there, but now doing very well. This magnificent falcon has actually learned how to search for food by night when its urban prey is more likely to be active instead of its traditional forays for food by day. And the seagull now living in cities provides safety for its offspring from urban predators by building its nest using trash from the streets below. This adaptation of urban animals can be compared with the adaptation of humans themselves about ten thousand years ago, when they developed as a society from being hunter-gatherers to a much more geographically stable system dependent upon agriculture. This process led initially to lower life expectancies, in part because the diet of these early humans became less varied and thus, ironically, less healthy. In addition, as humans began to live in ever more dense population centers, disease increased significantly. But over several thousand years, new human gene variants slowly allowed them to cope with these threats to their very existence. Special urban biodiversity projects are being set up in a number of big cities across the world, including Toronto and Singapore, where inhabitants are being encouraged to create a record of the biodiversity in their environment. Glasgow has recently launched a plan for volunteers from interested community groups to record information using surveys to determine residents' ideas about how to increase local biodiversity. Gathering such data has led to a variety of schemes promoting wildlife. In the UK, a group called Biodiversity Strategy is conducting a special program to encourage the introduction of thousands more trees in urban areas because of their particular suitability as shelter for large numbers of wildlife species. Certain animals, including most famously rats and pigeons, have adapted incredibly successfully to cities, and in fact have done so well in some instances that they have become nuisances and a hazard to health. Likewise, among plants, some weeds often adjust well to urban life, much to the annoyance of landscape specialists and gardeners. Many urban dwellers will tolerate nature only if they can control it and if it is relatively clean, not messy or random. In other words, if wildlife is not truly wild.

That is the end of Part 4. You now have forty-five seconds to check your answers to Part 4.

analyses.content: 录音中提到野生动物在农村地区受到狩猎的威胁，对应题目中 rural areas 的威胁。
录音先说了 farms and housing，但那属于“另一个威胁”，不要把这里提到的狩猎和后面的房屋建设混淆。

Sometimes species survive more successfully than in rural areas where they may be threatened by hunting, though this is increasingly regulated by governments. Another threat they face in rural areas is the ever-encroaching spread of farms and suburban housing, which reduces natural habitat significantly.
录音明确列举了旧建筑上有苔藓、地衣，且特别提到了昆虫在那里找地方繁衍和栖息。
你可能注意到了 moss 和 lichens，但题目空缺处需要的是同样依附于建筑的另一类生物。
There are moss and lichens on older buildings, and particularly numerous are the insects which find breeding places and shelter there.
录音提到环境学家很早就注意到花园围墙能吸引植物和小型动物，此处对应 garden 的围墙。
录音中提到了很多花园墙的材质，如 wood, stone, brick 等，但只有 wall 是涵盖这些材质的概括词。

And urban environmentalists have for a long time been aware of the particular attraction of garden walls made of wood, stone, brick, and even concrete, which provide ideal spots for smaller plant and animal species to thrive.
录音提到伦敦的游隼学会了在夜间寻找食物，因为此时猎物更活跃。
录音提到了传统的白天觅食方式（day），但题目问的是它现在觅食的时间点，注意排除对比干扰。
This magnificent falcon has actually learned how to search for food by night when its urban prey is more likely to be active instead of its traditional forays for food by day.
录音说明海鸥通过利用街道上的垃圾来筑巢，从而保护后代免受城市天敌侵害。
录音提到垃圾（trash）是用来筑“nest”的材料，不要错填成垃圾。
And the seagull now living in cities provides safety for its offspring from urban predators by building its nest using trash from the streets below.
录音对比人类十千年前的改变，指出人类社会从狩猎采集转向了依赖农业（agriculture）的稳定系统。
录音中提到了 hunter-gatherers，但这是过去的状态，题目问的是“基于什么”，要选择农业。

This adaptation of urban animals can be compared with the adaptation of humans themselves about ten thousand years ago, when they developed as a society from being hunter-gatherers to a much more geographically stable system dependent upon agriculture.
录音解释随着人类进入高密度居住区，疾病（disease）的传播显著增加。
虽然句中提到了 diet 和 life expectancies，但导致人口密集区问题的直接原因是疾病。
In addition, as humans began to live in ever more dense population centers, disease increased significantly.
录音提到志愿者使用调查（surveys）来收集信息，以确定当地增加生物多样性的想法。
录音中提到了 record information，要找的是实现这一目的的工具手段，即 surveys。
Glasgow has recently launched a plan for volunteers from interested community groups to record information using surveys to determine residents' ideas about how to increase local biodiversity.
录音提到英国的 Biodiversity Strategy 计划在城市种植数千棵更多的树木，因为它们非常适合作为野生动物的栖息地。
不要混淆题目中的“目标数量”与计划增加的“对象”，目标是增加树的数量。

In the UK, a group called Biodiversity Strategy is conducting a special program to encourage the introduction of thousands more trees in urban areas because of their particular suitability as shelter for large numbers of wildlife species.
录音指出像老鼠和鸽子这样的动物在城市过度适应，以至于变成了健康（health）的危害。
录音中提到了 nuisances（麻烦），但题目要求对应“对……造成危险”，health 才是填空的核心对象。

Certain animals, including most famously rats and pigeons, have adapted incredibly successfully to cities, and in fact have done so well in some instances that they have become nuisances and a hazard to health.
